newsitem.title: BRAZIL: IMF criticizes Brazil auto import rules-paper.
newsitem.headline: IMF criticizes Brazil auto import rules-paper.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has criticized Brazil's protectionist auto import policy, saying it is not needed to curb the country's trade deficit, O Estado de S. Paulo newspaper said.

O Estado reported the IMF study could be used to back up a World Trade Organization probe into the country's auto regime, which is currently being challenged by the European Union, Japan, South Korea and the United States.

The rules, created in 1995, benefit automakers and autoparts manufacturers operating in Brazil by allowing them to import cheaper equipment and components while imposing a 70-percent car import tariff for firms with no local base.
The IMF said the country could easily finance its trade gap with its large foreign reserves if the auto regime were lifted, according to O Estado.

In addition to the rules, the Brazilian government recently approved a controversial decree granting tax and import tariff breaks to entice auto investment to the country's impoverished north and northeast.
The latest move triggered protests by the Argentine government, which said it would draw badly needed auto investment away from Argentina and Mercosur partners Paraguay and Uruguay.

Meanwhile, Gazeta Mercantil newspaper reported that a group of lawyers who specialize in Mercosur have proposed the creation of an independent body to regulate incentives in the region and guarantee fair competition.
